title: Geometry - Lesson 1 Assessment: Modeling Geometric Terms
description: Show mastery by identifying, naming, and explaining foundational geometric terms and notation.

questions.question: Which term is defined as part of a line with two endpoints?
questions.explanation: A segment is the part of a line between two endpoints.

questions.question: Which notation means the line through points C and D?
questions.explanation: A line symbol has arrows in both directions over the two point labels.

questions.question: A plane is modeled by a flat surface, but a mathematical plane extends forever.
questions.explanation: A real flat surface is only a model. In geometry, a plane has no thickness and extends without end.

questions.question: A ray named $\overrightarrow{MN}$ starts at point ______.
questions.explanation: The first letter in ray notation names the endpoint.

questions.question: Which pair is made only of defined terms?
questions.explanation: Rays and angles can be defined using points and lines. Point, line, and plane are undefined terms.

questions.question: In $\angle RST$, which rays form the angle?
questions.explanation: The vertex is S, so both rays must start at S: ray SR and ray ST.

questions.question: Three collinear points are enough to name exactly one plane.
questions.explanation: Three non-collinear points determine a plane. If the points are collinear, many planes can contain that line.

questions.question: Give one real-life model for a ray and explain why it fits.
questions.correctAnswer: A flashlight beam can model a ray because it starts at the flashlight and travels outward in one direction.
questions.explanation: A strong answer identifies one starting point and one direction of extension.

questions.question: Explain the difference between an undefined term and a defined term in geometry. Include one example of each.
questions.correctAnswer: An undefined term is a starting idea that is described rather than defined from earlier terms, such as point. A defined term is built from earlier ideas, such as a segment.
questions.explanation: The key idea is that point, line, and plane are foundational, while segment, ray, and angle are built from them.

questions.question: A student draws $\overrightarrow{AB}$ but puts the endpoint at B and the arrow past A. What should be corrected?
questions.correctAnswer: The endpoint should be at A, and the ray should pass through B and continue beyond B.
questions.explanation: For ray AB, A is the endpoint and B shows the direction.
